title: Top-Account Backlog Liquidity Engine and Negotiated Delivery Cadence
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Problem: High-touch top-account asks routinely clog the public roadmap backlog and cause reactive re-prioritization of engineering sprints. We need a mechanism to surface, quantify, and liquidate top-account demand into timeboxed, negotiable delivery commitments that preserve SLA integrity while keeping the product roadmap predictable.

Proposal: Build a Backlog Liquidity Engine (BLE) — a lightweight, auditable system that converts account signals (escalations, committed pilots, renewal risk, legal blocking) into a set of negotiable delivery slots. Each slot has a bandwidth (points), an earliest delivery window, and an uptake policy (trade-offs: scope reduction, partial deliverable, consultancy vs product change). The BLE couples with the customer intake UI in Console and a small routing policy service to recommend lanes: Fastpass (tight SLA, paid reserved capacity), Negotiated (timeboxed trade-off), and Backlog (standard queue).

Key outcomes: (1) reduce emergency roadmap interrupts by 40% for mid-quarter escalations, (2) improve on-time delivery for committed enterprise features by 25%, (3) create traceable commitments for sales/CS to manage expectations.
acceptance_criteria: BLE converts incoming top-account signals into a ranked set of slots with metadata (points, window, proposed trade-off) visible in Console
Console UI allows PM or AE to propose a negotiated cadence and capture the acceptance terms; entries are exported to customer agreements or CS notes
Routing service integrates with Dedicated autoscale policies to optionally reserve burst capacity for accepted Fastpass slots
Reporting dashboard shows per-account slot history, realized delivery, and rework/rollback rates
Automated guardrails prevent >30% of sprint capacity being reserved for negotiated slots without engineering sign-off
notes: Trade-offs: conservative defaults for points allocation to avoid starving product-led roadmap; escalate to ENG if slot reservations exceed threshold
We intentionally decouple BLE from billing in Phase 1; billing is a follow-up once negotiation semantics stabilize
Design will reuse existing intake form fields and extend with a 'negotiation template' to speed agreement capture
Legal/Commercial should review proposed acceptance language for partial deliverables (action: @Sarah Lin)
Alignment: maps to OKR 2026.Q2 Objective C: "reduce enterprise churn through commitment clarity"
